summary: Extended /Users/imyu/.claude/orchestrator/hooks/classify.sh to nudge user on first message of a session if ready tasks or stale loops exist. Added a block immediately after the orch-off gate check that: (1) uses a /tmp/orch-first-msg-seen-{SID} marker file to fire only once per session; (2) queries localhost:8787/ready (max-time 0.5s) and counts ready tasks; (3) queries localhost:8787/loop/status (max-time 0.5s) and counts real+swept inactive loops; (4) injects combined additionalContext nudge if either count >0, then exits 0; (5) falls through silently if daemon is down, returns bad JSON, or no ready tasks/loops exist. Verified: correct JSON output with live daemon (4 ready tasks + 7 stale loops), graceful silent fallback when daemon is down, and deduplication via marker file.

subject: classify.sh: nudge user on session start if ready tasks or stale loops exist
description: In classify.sh (UserPromptSubmit hook), add a check on the FIRST message of a session: query the daemon for ready tasks and stale/inactive loops. If any exist, inject an additionalContext nudge asking the user if they want to resume (e.g. "3 tasks ready from last session — reply 'resume' to pick them up"). Should be idempotent (only fire once per session, not on every message).

summary: classify.sh extended with first-message-per-session nudge: checks /ready and /loop/status, injects ready-task count + stale-loop count into additionalContext. Silent on daemon-down. Marker file /tmp/orch-first-msg-seen-{SID} prevents re-firing.
